_doc: Rules from Analista/Rastreador research docs. gate.py enforces every rule here before any publish. A solved research doc whose actions are not covered here must get a rule added BEFORE producing. Never delete a rule unless its research doc is 'failed' and a replacement rule exists.

rules.text: Never upload the same video file twice to the same platform (no delete-and-reupload).
Max 3 TikToks per calendar day (America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires), at least 3 h between publish/schedule times.
Content Check Lite in TikTok Studio read before posting; if it warns 'Content may be restricted', do NOT post: change the video and run the gate again.
rules.disabled_by: Felipe por mail 27/11 11:20: 'continúa con todo lo demás' — solo se puede hacer a mano en YouTube/TikTok Studio; no bloquea la publicación en la nube

rules.text: 'Creator labeled as AI-generated' turned on.
Experiment: the first TikTok of each day has no mention of YouTube in its caption (CTA spoken only).
Spoken hook starts at 0.0 s: leading silence <= 0.15 s.
Hook text on screen from frame 1: first caption chunk starts <= 0.3 s.
Spoken hook (first sentence of the script) is 10 words or fewer.
No logo, title card or slow camera move in the first 2 s (check the frame-1 still).
Do not judge, delete or edit-repost a TikTok before 24 h; earlier TikToks of the batch were left untouched.
First frame is the most striking image of the story (not an establishing shot), with the hook as on-screen text (check the frame-1 still).
Publish/schedule time (--at) must be one of the slots the Rastreador set in studio/schedule.json for that platform and format.
Shorts last 30-60 s (never the 100+ s cuts that got 0.4% completion on TikTok).
Right after the YouTube video (short or episode) is live, pin our own comment with one concrete question about the new lore clue (e.g. 'What do you think is on T. Rowe's memory card?').

rules.text: The caption asks the viewer one concrete question about the story (contains '?'), e.g. 'Would you cut the line?'.
Reel meets Buffer auto-publish limits: 3 s-15 min, <=300 MB, aspect between 4:5 and 9:16, <=1920 px wide.

Buffer post is type reel with automatic publishing (not notification publishing); afterwards get_post shows status sent with the Instagram link. Every short also goes to Instagram Reels, plus the episode Part 1.

Each YouTube Short has its 'Related video' set to the episode of the same story (YouTube Studio > Short > Related video). Links in Shorts descriptions are not clickable, so the description link alone sends nobody to the episode.

rules.text: Narration made with the user's chosen voice (studio/voice.json: Chatterbox default voice) through the TTS workflow: narration/<ID>/ must hold .json markers with engine chatterbox.

No post is recorded (gate.py record) unless its compliance report says pass:true, covers every rule enabled at that moment and was checked for the same publish time. S07 Instagram went out with GATE FAIL and S07-S09 TikTok with a report from before R12/R13/R15 existed (r004, r006).

If the last 3 TikToks with 24 h Buffer metrics all have 0 views, no new TikTok is scheduled for 7 days after the newest of them (keep producing for YouTube and Instagram). r001 failed: R1-R5 did not bring views back.

Once each TikTok has views, write its viewer countries (Windsor tiktok_organic video_audience_countries) in research doc r009. Do not change the account region, language or device to chase a country: only one variable at a time (experiment in r009).
Shorts: a new image and a new fact (reveal) land between 5 and 8 s; no explanation or set-up sentence after the hook. YouTube Shorts lost most viewers between 22% and 38% of their length (s 6-11).
At most 2 YouTube posts through Buffer in any 24 h (Buffer free plan limit for YouTube Shorts). A 3rd post waits for the next free slot.

The YouTube episode is uploaded through the YouTube API workflow (repo GitHub Actions, same secrets as youtube_meta.yml), not through Buffer, so Buffer's 2 daily YouTube posts go to Shorts. If the upload workflow does not exist yet, build it before publishing the episode.
